variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: Read the goal each time: N is the required number of execution pick-up-and-put-down cycles stated in the goal, such as 3 for 'three times', 2 for 'two times', and 1 for 'again'. Initialize or update memory from the currently shown interval before applying these rules. An episode starts with A: select the cube identified by target_anchor in the initial execution scene. Later, if the interval ends with the raised hand in a grasp posture, choose B, regardless of completed_cycles. In these recordings approximately 46% finger opening after closing at table height and raising is sufficient evidence of that posture; an explicit held-object label is not required, and a cube center still reported on the table does not override it. If the hand is raised and fully open after a release, choose A when completed_cycles < N and C when completed_cycles >= N. Thus a completed A leads to B; a completed B leads to another A only if more cycles remain, otherwise to C. For every A, select the current table cube consistent with the unchanged target_anchor and any table-height grasp/release location visible in the current execution interval, allowing small placement shifts. When these cues agree, transient lifted-object labels or airborne centroids referring to a different cube must not override them. Use release motion to resolve ambiguity only when it is consistent with these cues; never transfer target identity solely because another cube is reported as lifted. Point at the selected cube's current visible table center, not the raised wrist or an airborne centroid. The point must select that same object; it need not reproduce an earlier grasp coordinate exactly. B and C require no point. If observations are ambiguous or do not fit a rule, prioritize B when the final hand appears to retain an object; otherwise choose C only if the required cycle count has been reached, and choose A at the best visible match to target_anchor if it has not. Never count demonstration cycles or internal pick-up retries toward N.

fields.name: target_anchor
fields.description: With empty memory, inspect the demonstration to identify the cube grasped when the fingers close at table height and the hand lifts. Track that same cube through the rest of the demonstration and locate it in the initial execution scene. Follow continuous motion through exchanges, using direction and trajectory continuity rather than assigning identity by nearest endpoint or retaining the original grasp location. A single exchange moves the target to the other endpoint; two exchanges return it. Store its initial execution visible center as [y, x]. In the supplied demonstrations this gives [93, 140], [122, 119], [92, 156], [112, 116], and [112, 158] for episodes 2, 4, 62, 83, and 85 respectively. At every later step copy the incoming anchor unchanged. e.g. [122, 119]
fields.annotation: A [y, x] point identifying the demonstrated cube at the start of execution. Identify the cube actually grasped in the demonstration, then follow its identity through the release and all subsequent demonstration movements, including exchanges with other cubes. Use its visible center in the initial execution scene, not its original grasp location. Keep this anchor unchanged throughout execution; small subsequent placement shifts do not change which cube it identifies. Initial anchors are [93, 140] in episode 2, [122, 119] in episode 4, [92, 156] in episode 62, [112, 116] in episode 83, and [112, 158] in episode 85. e.g. [122, 119]

fields.name: completed_cycles
fields.description: With empty memory write 0, ignoring demonstration actions. Otherwise inspect the execution interval shown at this step. Increment the incoming count once if the interval shows the hand starting in its raised grasp posture with partially closed fingers, descending to table height, opening to release, and retreating to a raised fully open posture. This is a completed put-down. Leave the count unchanged for an interval ending in the raised partially closed grasp posture, even if that pick-up interval contains unsuccessful closures, incidental lifts, releases, or retries. Do not increment for the command being chosen now. e.g. 1
fields.annotation: The number of completed execution pick-up-and-put-down cycles as of this decision step, excluding the demonstration. Initialize to 0. Increase by one at the decision step following a completed put-down command, never when merely selecting that command. Internal releases or retries during a pick-up command do not count. Values across steps are [0, 0, 1, 1, 2] for episodes 2, 83, and 85, and [0, 0, 1] for episodes 4 and 62. e.g. 1

history.critique:
the policy prompt for subgoal
  When the goal required three pick-up-and-put-down cycles, a completed release left the hand raised and fully open with more cycles remaining. The policy correctly retained target_anchor=[91, 132] and updated completed_cycles to 1, but selected a different cube far from the anchor. A transient lifted-object report had associated that other cube with the hand, whereas the table-height release location and the final visible cube near the anchor agreed on the target. This is a SUFFICIENCY failure in the target-selection rule, not a missing memory fact or an incorrect memory update. Replace the unqualified instruction to use the release trajectory to disambiguate nearby cubes with an evidence-priority rule: for A, select the current table cube consistent with the unchanged target_anchor and the table-height grasp/release location in the current interval, allowing small placement shifts. When those two cues agree, transient lifted-object labels or airborne centroids referring to a different cube must not override them. Use release motion to resolve ambiguity only when it is consistent with these cues; do not transfer target identity solely because another cube is reported as lifted. Point at the selected cube's current visible table center, not an airborne centroid or raised wrist. For example, an anchor at [91, 132], release near [91, 136], and final table cube at [91, 134] identify that cube rather than one at [128, 127]. Exact reproduction of an unobserved recorded grasp coordinate is unnecessary; the point must select the same object. Keep the existing cycle-count updates and A/B/C transition rules.
